text.title: sql-optimization Failure Modes
text.summary: Seven failure modes observed when applying the sql-optimization methodology. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Engineer adds 5 indexes 'to be safe' without an EXPLAIN baseline; write latency triples.
antipattern.fix: Drop unjustified indexes; gate every CREATE INDEX on an EXPLAIN ANALYZE diff.

antipattern.symptom: Team optimizes a nightly batch query (10s once a day) instead of the 100ms-x-10K/day path that dominates p95.
antipattern.fix: Use slow-query log + pg_stat_statements to rank by total_time = mean_time * calls; optimize top-N.

antipattern.symptom: Optimized query still SELECT *; covering index never kicks in.
antipattern.fix: Replace SELECT * with explicit column list aligned to the covering index.

antipattern.symptom: Bulk load of 10M rows; optimizer keeps old stats; new query uses a seqscan instead of the new index.
antipattern.fix: Run ANALYZE table_name after the bulk load; verify with EXPLAIN.

antipattern.symptom: The plan shows `rows=10` where `actual rows=1000000`. The planner picks a nested loop; the freshly added index changes nothing and the query stays slow.
antipattern.root-cause: Not the same failure as stale stats after a load — here the column's distribution is skewed enough that the default statistics target cannot describe it, so the estimate is wrong even after ANALYZE.
antipattern.fix: ANALYZE and re-EXPLAIN first. If the skew survives, raise the column's statistics target (`ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN c SET STATISTICS 1000`) and ANALYZE again before proposing any index. Rule investigate-row-estimate-skew.

antipattern.symptom: A composite index exists on `(created_at, tenant_id)` and the `tenant_id = ?` query still does a sequential scan. The index looks right in the schema and is never used.
antipattern.root-cause: The range/sort column was placed first, so the B-tree prefix is a timestamp — the equality predicate has no usable leading column.
antipattern.fix: Recreate as `(tenant_id, created_at DESC, id)` and confirm with EXPLAIN that the scan uses the tenant_id prefix. Rule composite-index-ordering; snippet in `templates/create_index_concurrently.sql`.

antipattern.symptom: A list endpoint returning 200 rows takes 8 seconds. `pg_stat_statements` shows the inner query executed 200 times for one outer call.
antipattern.root-cause: A correlated subquery sits in the SELECT list, so it runs once per outer row.
antipattern.fix: Rewrite as a JOIN with GROUP BY and an aggregate; verify a single execution in the new plan. Rule no-subquery-in-select.
